body: Found by the fuzzing pass (T-326), left out of its scope. The accounts unique index uses SQLite's ASCII-only lower(), so 'É@x.co' and 'é@x.co' can both register; invites.redeem matches the invited address with Python's full-Unicode .lower(), so both accounts can redeem the same invite, while pending_for uses SQLite lower() and offers it only to the exact-case account. Decide one folding (store a Python-casefolded email_normalized column, unique, used by every lookup; or restrict addresses to ASCII at registration, which the caps section could state) and document it in the wire contract. Non-ASCII local parts are rare; low priority.
title: Server: e-mail case folding differs between SQLite (ASCII lower) and Python (Unicode lower) outside ASCII
